newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to speed up sell-offs with new tenders.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to speed up sell-offs with new tenders.

text.p: Turkey is planning to speed up its sluggish 10-year-old sell-off programme with new tenders to be opened this year, Ismail Karakaya, chairman of the Privatisation Administration (OIB), said on Tuesday.
"Privatisation will be accelerated in the coming days...and the fruits of new tenders will be collected from the beginning of 1997," Karakaya told Reuters.
He said the administration would call for tenders for the privatisation of iron and steel producer Eregli and Etibank by the end of this year.
The OIB will also finalise studies for a tender to chose an adviser to run the privatisation of four power plants.
Karakaya said the OIB would put giant oil companies -- petrochemical firm Petkim, Tupras refining company and petroleum distributor Petrol Ofisi -- on sale early next year.
He did not say how much was expected to be raised from the latest selloffs.
The OIB will also privatise a cement factory in eastern Turkey, marinas of Turban tourism company and Karadeniz Copper Factories later this year.
Turkey has raised only $3 billion through sell-offs since the privatisation programme was launched in 1986 .
Earlier efforts to speed up sell-offs were hampered by court annulments, political turmoil and frequent reshuffles at senior OIB posts.
Karakaya said the new sell-off programme would be given to an International Monetary Fund (IMF) team which is presently examining the Turkish economy.

The IMF and World Bank urge Turkey to take structural measures and fasten privatisation to narrow huge public deficits, expected to reach 10 percent of the country's gross national product this year from 6.5 percent in 1995.
